acip: [E15] DE DAG LA KHYAB PA YOD DE, LUS LEN PA'I RNAM SHES NI SKYE BA SNGA MA'I LAS KYI MTHUS TSE JI SRID KYI BAR DU RGYUN MA CHAD PAR 'JUG PA'I RNAM SMIN YIN PA DANG, RTAG TU MA BSGRIBS LUNG MA BSTAN GYI NGO BOR GNAS PA DANG, TSE JI SRID KYI BAR DU LUS THAMS CAD LA KHYAB NAS 'DZIN PA ZHIG DGOS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
wylie: [e15] de dag la khyab pa yod de, lus len pa'i rnam shes ni skye ba snga ma'i las kyi mthus tshe ji srid kyi bar du rgyun ma chad par 'jug pa'i rnam smin yin pa dang, rtag tu ma bsgribs lung ma bstan gyi ngo bor gnas pa dang, tshe ji srid kyi bar du lus thams cad la khyab nas 'dzin pa zhig dgos pa'i phyir ro
english: There is a logical necessity within these arguments because, first of all, the consciousness that takes on the body should be one that represents a ripening of karma which occurs through the power of karma committed in a previous lifetime, and should continue on in an unbroken stream for the duration of our life.  Moreover, its fundamental nature should be karmically neutral, of the type which does not cause any spiritual obstacle.  And lastly it should hold its objects even as it extends over the entire body—again for the entire length of our life. Second argument: How could one arise first?
